minutes.headline: Planning Board approved a Stone Farm duplex change, waived three Elmwood rules, and shaped a marijuana bylaw.
minutes.summary: The board approved splitting a four-unit Stone Farm building into two duplexes, then took up the Elmwood Road subdivision and granted three of five waivers, holding two for Conservation Commission input. Most of the evening went to a draft medical marijuana bylaw, with leanings toward referencing state rules, a retail overlay in the commercial area and growing allowed in several districts. Special permit versus by-right stayed open. Members also asked to hear from DPW, the town manager and town counsel about who maintains subdivision drainage.

votes.motion: Accept the proposed modification to the Stone Farm project, changing a four-unit building into duplexes.
Approve the Elmwood tree plan waiver on condition that trees are shown on the site plan.
Grant the tabular summary waiver for Elmwood.
Waive the sidewalks on the Elmwood development.
Approve the minutes of the January 27th regular meeting.
Approve the minutes of the January 27th information meeting.
Approve the minutes of the January 6th public hearing on the special town meeting article.
Approve the minutes of the December 8th site visit to the Lane property on Holman Street.

decisions.decision: Two Elmwood waivers (environmental impact statement and the road length) are held until the Conservation Commission meets on February 19th.
Staff will arrange a meeting with the DPW director, the town manager and town counsel on stormwater maintenance in new subdivisions.
The marijuana bylaw will reference state regulations rather than repeat them.
General agreement on a retail overlay in the Mass Ave and Route 13 commercial area, with growing allowed in industrial and other districts under restrictions.
Members will email questions for town counsel to Marjorie, to go to counsel by Thursday. Staff will start a skeleton draft bylaw for the February 24th meeting, using the Concord example.
The proposal for extra meetings or workshops is tabled until next month.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board took up a draft medical marijuana bylaw and agreed it will reference state regulations rather than repeat them.
Members generally agreed on a retail overlay in the Mass Ave and Route 13 commercial area, with growing allowed in industrial and other districts under restrictions.
The board granted three Elmwood Road waivers, including the tree plan and sidewalks, but held two until the Conservation Commission meets February 19th.
A motion to change a four-unit Stone Farm building into duplexes was taken up; the minutes do not record an audible vote result.
Staff will arrange a meeting with the DPW director, town manager and town counsel on who maintains stormwater systems in new subdivisions.

why_it_matters: The marijuana bylaw will decide where in town retail and growing can locate, and whether each needs a special permit or is allowed by right, a choice still open.
Who maintains drainage in new subdivisions determines whether those costs fall on the town budget, mostly taxes, or on developers and homeowners.
Vote results for the Stone Farm and Elmwood motions were not audible in the recording, so the outcomes rest on the board's decisions as summarized.
watch_next: Conservation Commission meeting on February 19th, which bears on the two held Elmwood waivers.
Planning Board meeting on February 24th, where staff will present a skeleton marijuana bylaw based on the Concord example.
